facts.fact: The Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT), the second national ICT policy after the 2005 one, states it was approved by Cabinet on 10 August 2016.
facts.system: Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

facts.fact: The full policy text, with foreword by the Minister of ICT, Postal and Courier Services, is circulated openly as a PDF distributed by Veritas and hosted on a government policy portal; the document gives no other date, so the approval date is used.
facts.system: Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

facts.fact: The policy sets dated targets (top 3 in Africa on the ICT Development Index by 2018, universal access with 80% geographic coverage by 2018) and lists scopes of work per programme and a results-actions-outcomes table, but states no cost or budget for any of them.
facts.system: Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

facts.fact: The policy names the Ministry of Information Communication Technology, Postal and Courier Services as its driver and coordinator, and provides for national advisory committees to be set up by the Ministry; it states no standing delivery body already operating.
facts.system: Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

facts.fact: The policy states no allocation for its own implementation; it says programmes are to be funded through the normal business plans of state enterprises and the private sector, and records that its 2012 review was supported financially by UNECA and the National Economic Consultative Forum.
facts.system: Zimbabwe National Policy for Information and Communications Technology (ICT)
